chunks: Ibn Mahboub, from Ibrahim ibn Nu'aym al-Azdi, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about four who testified against a man for adultery. So when he was killed, one of them retracted from his testimony. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The fourth one is killed, and the three pay three-quarters of the blood money to his family.'
ai.seo_question: What is the penalty when one of four witnesses to adultery retracts their testimony after the accused is executed?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the principle of 'shahid al-shuhud' (witness of witnesses) in Shia jurisprudence, where the retraction of one witness invalidates the collective testimony, leading to the execution of the retracting witness as a penalty for false testimony. The ruling distinguishes between the liability of the three remaining witnesses, who pay three-quarters of the diya, reflecting the proportional responsibility for the error in judgment. This case highlights the rigorous standards of evidence in Hadd punishments and the concept of vicarious liability in judicial errors.

en.hubeali: Ibn Mahboub, from Ibrahim Bin Nuaym Al Azdy who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about four who testified upon a man with the adultery. So when he was killed, one of them retracted from hits testimony. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The fourth one would be killed, and the (other) three would pay three-quarters of the wergild to his family’.
